newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian woman tells of surviving firing squad.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian woman tells of surviving firing squad.

text.p: A woman hit by 10 bullets who survived execution by firing squad in Ethiopia 18 years ago told a court on Wednesday how she so narrowly escaped death.
The woman was a prosecution witness at the trial of 71 former officials of Ethiopia's former Marxist military junta, known as the Dergue, which ruled from 1974 to its overthrow in 1991.
The 71 are accused of genocide and human rights violations.

"About 40 of us were rounded up and held in jail for participating in a protest march against the rule of Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam on April 12, 1979," the woman, who under court rules cannot be identified, told the court.
"After we were kept in jail for some time, 40 of us were tied in pairs and were driven to a suburb of Addis Ababa known as Sululta late one evening in 1979," she added.

"We were ordered to dismount from the truck and were lined up near an earth mound, where gunmen who escorted us to the spot opened fire at point blank range, killing everyone except me," she said as the accused grimly listened to her testimony.
"I was hit by 10 bullets and was drenched in blood. I was still conscious so I untied my hand from the dead girl to whom I was tied and rolled down into a nearby bush where I hid," she said.
She said she spent the night warding off howling hyenas. In the morning she crawled to a highway where a woman found her and drove her to the Black Lion hospital where her brother was a doctor.
Her brother was later executed by the Dergue for hiding and aiding an opposition party member. She showed the court scars from her wounds and said she was now healthy but had persistent headaches.
Only 46 of the 71 former Marxist officials were in the dock on Wednesday. The others including Mengistu, who ruled from 1977 to 1991 and now lives in exile in Zimbabwe, are being tried in absentia.
Their trial was adjourned until October 7. Ethiopia has charged 5,198 former officials with genocide and war crimes.
